All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable, robocode.robotinterfaces.IAdvancedEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IAdvancedRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicEvents2, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicEvents3, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.IInteractiveEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IInteractiveRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.IPaintEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IPaintRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.ITeamEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.ITeamRobot
public class HadurRecorder extends Hadur
Hadur, plus a transcript of every input and order in Replay's format. The bench runs it with Robocode's security off to capture replay fixtures (CORE-2); it is left out of the competition jar.

The transcript goes to the file named by the hadur.record system property.

The transcript is the format Replay.run(java.util.List<java.lang.String>, hadur2.core.port.Telemetry) reads: an F line when the battle starts, an N line at each round's start, then for every turn the I line of the input the core was given and the O line of the orders it returned, both from LineCodec. Replaying it through a fresh core must give the same orders tick for tick (CORE-2).

A0 (STRAND-4) adds the lines a replay needs to run the adapter's memory calls too, and to check the files they leave. Replay ignores them; the tests' fixture replay reads them. They are re-derived here, in the recorder's own handlers, from the same getters and in the same order Hadur uses, so the shipped adapter is unchanged:

  • Q,quota and one D,name,lastModified,base64 per file in the data directory, before the F line: the store the battle started on;
  • RE,tick,result,energy: the adapter's one roundEnded call of a round (the guard's fault count is the replay's own);
  • CP,tick: the round-end checkpoint, made only while Hadur is alive;
  • BE,tick and HE,rounds,survived,skippedTurns: the battle-end save and the health record's arguments (faults again the replay's own);
  • one S,name,base64 per file the battle left in the data directory.

A5 (STRAND-5): on a team each member writes its own transcript, the property's file name with -member-N before its extension, N from the engine's (N) suffix on the member's name. Its F line carries the rest of the battle's facts, F,width,height,others,name,startingEnergy,sentryBorder,mate;mate;..., and it writes no store lines: the members share one data directory, which only the leader writes (SHELF-2), so no member's store is its own to replay.

This class writes a file outside the data directory with plain java.nio, which Robocode's sandbox would forbid, hence security off. Any I/O failure is thrown as UncheckedIOException.
